# The converter's environment: the packages bge-m3's conversion ran with (models.lock,
# converter.packages), each with the sha256 of every file PyPI has for it. `clarity fetch`
# installs them into models/.converter with `uv pip install --require-hashes --no-build`, so
# a file that doesn't match is refused and only wheels are installed. Linux adds PyPI
# torch's NVIDIA libraries and triton, and Windows tqdm's colorama. Made by listing that
# record as NAME==VERSION lines in PINS, then:
#   uv pip compile PINS --universal --python-version 3.13 --generate-hashes --no-header --no-annotate
# For a new llama.cpp pin, PINS is instead the requirement lines of llama.cpp's
# requirements/requirements-convert_hf_to_gguf.txt and the file its -r line names, without
# its --extra-index-url line (the conversions ran with PyPI's torch), plus
# sentencepiece==0.2.2 (0.2.3 needs protobuf 5, which those files rule out), then:
#   uv pip compile PINS --no-config --default-index https://pypi.org/simple --universal
#     --python-version 3.13 --generate-hashes --no-header --no-annotate
# A live test checks that these pins meet llama.cpp's requirements at its pinned commit.
